The paper compares backprojection and iterative smooth reweighted L1-minimization methods for analyzing RCS measurement data using ISAR imaging.
Backprojection is a straightforward and robust method, but is limited by the resolution of the measurement setup.
The L1-minimization method can provide better resolution than backprojection, allowing for RCS extraction of more closely spaced scatterers.
The L1-minimization method is less accurate than backprojection in extracting the true RCS values, especially for closely spaced scatterers.
The simulations used a frequency range of 13.5-16.5 GHz in 41 steps and an azimuth angle range of -5.7° to 5.7° in 41 steps.
The down-range resolution of the simulations was 5 cm, defined by the frequency bandwidth.
The reweighting matrix W in the L1-minimization method was calculated as W = 1 / (xD + η), where xD is a smoothed version of the image x and η is a small value.
Four iterations of the L1-minimization with reweighting were performed for all examples shown in the paper.
The main conclusion is that backprojection is more robust and accurate for RCS extraction, but the L1-minimization method can provide better resolution for closely spaced scatterers.
The L1-minimization method should be preferred when the scattering features cannot be resolved in the backprojection image.
The paper presents and discusses the pros and cons of the two methods in terms of resolution, accuracy, and applicability.
The point scattering model is defined in the forward operator A and the backward operator A^T, which are used to solve the inverse problem.
The problem to be solved is formulated as a minimization of the L1-norm of the image x subject to a constraint on the L2-norm of the residual Ax-y.
The iterative smooth reweighted L1-minimization procedure is adapted from previous work on sparse reconstruction and cluster-sparsity problems.
The smoothing function D is used to create a smoothed version of the image x, which is then used to calculate the reweighting matrix W.
